title: Genshin Impact — Item Story
style_tags: premium Genshin-style anime cel-shaded fantasy frame, clean elegant linework, vibrant saturated colors, painterly Inazuma and Snezhnaya environments, cinematic dramatic lighting, restrained magenta Tatarigami energy only where canon requires it, detailed metal and cord materials, edge-to-edge vertical 9:16 composition, no photorealism, no 3D product render, no game UI, no inventory card, no text overlay

format_overrides.narrative_mode: An external lore narrator tells the canonical item's history in third person. The item never narrates as I, me, or my. Canon establishes that this blade possessed consciousness before its final reforging, but the narration still speaks about it from outside.
format_overrides.visual_priority: The sword is the largest, sharpest, and most unobstructed focal subject in every clip. Makers and wielders appear only as hands, torso crops, silhouettes, or secondary figures without identity-critical faces.
format_overrides.structure: HOOK (the cursed blade crossed nations by possessing wielders) → FORGING IN SNEZHNAYA → JOURNEY TO INAZUMA → POWER SPENT / ENCOUNTER WITH KAZUHA → FINAL REFORGING → CONSCIOUSNESS LOST / LEGACY → CTA
format_overrides.state_continuity: All three states retain the same long, slender, slightly curved single-edged silhouette, angular layered guard, wrapped grip, and flared pommel. Only the blade's energy pattern, surface brightness, wear, and guard finish change at canon-supported cuts.
format_overrides.owner_visibility: Kazuha may be named in narration, but without an exact Item Story-owned character ref the image must show only anonymous red-and-black-sleeved hands, a cropped torso, or a backlit silhouette with no recognizable face. Akame Kanenaga is also shown without a recognizable face.

voice_policy.intent: low controlled masculine lore narrator, somber and intimate, measured dark-fantasy documentary delivery, restrained emotion, never shouting and never imitating a Genshin character
voice_policy.note: One consistent external narrator speaks about Kagotsurube Isshin in third person. Do not use a character voice clone.

music_policy.mood: tragic Inazuman dark fantasy crossing into cold Snezhnayan melancholy, restrained shamisen-like plucks, low strings, sparse ceremonial percussion, ominous magenta-energy tension resolving into quiet acceptance, no vocals

Secondary material and brightness check for the final form; the episode uses the base/reward appearance as the locked final state rather than depicting an unexplained ascension.
Primary appearance source for the awakened cursed state and its magenta luminous pattern. Research input only.
Primary appearance source for the power-spent battered state. The icon remains full-length, so do not depict a blade snapped into separate halves.
Chronology verification for the blade's arrival in Inazuma, confrontation with Kazuha, final reforging, revealed name, and loss of consciousness. Do not quote quest dialogue verbatim.

items.category: a cursed Inazuman single-edged sword forged in Snezhnaya and later reforged by Kaedehara Kazuha
items.canon_scope: Genshin Impact game canon from Kaedehara Kazuha's Story Quest, Acer Palmatum Chapter: Act I, plus the in-game weapon and quest-item descriptions. Do not invent later owners or events beyond the released quest endpoint.

appearance_lock.overall_shape: A long, slender, slightly curved single-edged Inazuman sword with a narrow dark blade and a long pointed, subtly upswept tip. The same elegant silhouette persists in all three states. No scabbard appears in the episode.
appearance_lock.guard: An unmistakable compact angular guard built from overlapping wing-, leaf-, or feather-like plates rather than a circular tsuba. A small triangular red or magenta insert sits at the blade base. The plates are dark brown-gray in cursed and battered states, becoming brighter silver-gray in the final state.
appearance_lock.grip: A long dark purple-black handle wrapped with pale silver diagonal cord that creates a repeated diamond pattern. In the awakened state the openings glow magenta; in the battered and final states they read pale silver over a dark core.
appearance_lock.pommel: A flared silver-gray metal end cap with angular sides and a small red inset or stripe. It is compact and aligned with the grip, never a large ornamental counterweight.
appearance_lock.blade_pattern: One flowing serpentine energy or hamon-like line sweeps almost the full blade length. It is intense luminous magenta-purple when awakened, pale white-silver and extinguished when power-spent, and vivid red-orange over a dark burgundy-black blade after the final reforging.
appearance_lock.scale_lock: A full-length one-handed sword: the blade is several times the grip length, and an adult hand wraps naturally around the narrow handle. It must never shrink into a knife or expand into an oversized broad fantasy greatsword.
appearance_lock.negative_lock: No generic katana, no gold circular tsuba, no blue or green blade, no straight medieval sword, no broad blade, no missing tip, no blade snapped into two pieces, no extra spikes, no readable runes or text, no scabbard, no product packshot, no floating inventory UI, and no generic flame weapon.

item_states.appearance: The full-length near-black blade carries an intense luminous magenta-purple serpentine line and restrained violet aura. The angular layered guard is dark brown-gray, the grip is dark with magenta diamond openings, and the silhouette remains slender and intact.

The same full-length silhouette after its power is exhausted: subdued dark burgundy-black blade, pale white-silver flowing line, gray-brown angular guard, pale handle wrap, scuffed and battered surfaces, no strong aura. It is worn and spiritually spent, not physically snapped in half.

The final reward form: a dark burgundy-purple to near-black blade crossed by a vivid red-orange flowing flame- or hamon-like stripe from base toward the pointed tip; bright silver-gray overlapping angular guard plates with a small red triangular insert; long dark grip with pale silver diamond-pattern wrapping; flared silver-gray pommel with a small red inset. No purple aura.

canonical_facts.fact: Akame Kanenaga, an Inazuman smith living in Snezhnaya, forged the blade from regret, a final wish to restore the Isshin Art's reputation, and Tatarigami malice.
canonical_facts.source: Kagotsurube Isshin and Prized Isshin Blade descriptions; Acer Palmatum Chapter: Act I

canonical_facts.fact: The blade possessed consciousness and used human hosts as tools while traveling toward Inazuma.
Its strength and aura greatly diminished by the time it reached Inazuma and encountered Kaedehara Kazuha.
canonical_facts.source: Prized Isshin Blade (Awakened/Shattered) descriptions; Acer Palmatum Chapter: Act I

canonical_facts.fact: Kazuha agreed to let the blade control his body for one final reforging attempt.
canonical_facts.source: Ere the End, a Glance Back

canonical_facts.fact: The reforging consumed the blade's remaining consciousness, after which it revealed the name Kagotsurube Isshin and remained with Kazuha as the story quest concluded.
canonical_facts.status: game canon narrative endpoint; the player also receives the weapon as a quest reward
canonical_facts.source: Ere the End, a Glance Back; Kagotsurube Isshin item acquisition

forbidden_claims: The final Kagotsurube Isshin still speaks, possesses wielders, or retains the cursed blade's consciousness after the reforging.
The power-spent blade was visibly snapped into two separate pieces.
Kazuha originally forged the cursed blade in Snezhnaya.
The blade is a five-star weapon or has a different in-game rarity than its canonical four-star status.
Its final red-orange pattern is flame magic or a Pyro Vision effect.
The ascended inventory render is a separate canonical reforging event in the story.

items.category: a five-star claymore whose name and iconography reference Andrius, the Wolf of the North, guardian spirit of Mondstadt's Wolvendom wolves
items.canon_scope: Genshin Impact game canon from the in-game weapon description and passive ability text, Wolvendom location content, and Razor's official character story and Story Quest 'Kindred by Blood'. Do not invent later owners or events beyond released content, and do not claim Andrius has died.

appearance_lock.overall_shape: A massive two-handed claymore with a broad, slightly asymmetrical double-tapered blade that widens toward the tip before narrowing to a blunt point; blade length roughly equal to an adult's torso plus outstretched arm. The same silhouette persists across all states.
appearance_lock.guard: A stylized wolf-fang guard: two curved, fang-like metal prongs flare outward from the blade base like a wolf's open jaw, flanking a small notched ridge. Dulled and corroded in the monument state, brighter silver-black in the current battle-ready state.
appearance_lock.grip: A long leather-wrapped hilt bound with iron chain links wound in a spiral, sized for a two-handed grip. Frayed in the monument state, freshly re-bound in the reclaimed and current states.
appearance_lock.surface_details: Shallow claw-mark grooves scored lengthwise down both faces of the blade, and a faint pale frost-blue rime or glow near the fuller that intensifies only when the weapon's passive is active.
appearance_lock.scale_lock: Full two-handed greatsword: blade length approximately matches an adult wielder's torso-to-fingertip reach; planted upright it stands roughly chest-to-shoulder height on an adult human. Never shrinks to one-handed size and never grows beyond one and a half times human height.
appearance_lock.negative_lock: No gold filigree, no curved katana or scimitar profile, no glowing color other than pale frost-blue or dull rust, no scabbard, no readable runic text, not a spear or polearm, no oversized fantasy proportions beyond the scale lock, no cartoon cracked-in-half blade.

item_states.appearance: A dulled grey grave-marker blade, wolf-fang guard pitted and green with corrosion, frayed chain-wrapped grip, no shine, faint claw-mark grooves filled with dried lichen, planted upright in frost-hardened Wolvendom earth like a headstone.

The same locked silhouette freshly pulled from the ground: blade scoured clean in patches but still rust-freckled near the guard, chain re-wound tighter, leather grip freshly re-bound over the old cord, frost-rime clinging near the fuller, carried loose in a gloved grip rather than planted.

The maintained present-day form: honed dark blued-grey steel catching cold light, wolf-fang guard polished silver-black, chain links tight and oiled, grip freshly leather-wrapped, pale frost-blue sheen pulsing along the etched claw-mark grooves when its passive triggers, held two-handed and battle-ready.

canonical_facts.fact: Wolf's Gravestone is a five-star claymore whose passive increases the wielder's ATK and, when a nearby enemy's HP falls below 30%, unleashes a shockwave dealing AoE physical DMG and granting the whole party a temporary ATK bonus.
canonical_facts.source: in-game weapon description and passive ability text

canonical_facts.fact: The weapon's name and wolf-fang iconography reference Andrius, the Wolf of the North King, the guardian spirit of the wild wolves living in Mondstadt's Wolvendom forest.
canonical_facts.source: in-game weapon flavor association; Wolvendom location lore

canonical_facts.fact: Wolvendom was the site of a prolonged conflict between Mondstadt's people and the wolves under Andrius's protection, as human settlement and hunting pushed into the wolves' territory.
canonical_facts.status: game canon (environmental storytelling and NPC dialogue in Wolvendom)
canonical_facts.source: Wolvendom location content; Razor character story

canonical_facts.fact: Razor, orphaned as a small child, was found and raised by Andrius's wolf pack in Wolvendom, and Andrius treats him as one of his own.
Razor's Story Quest, 'Kindred by Blood,' centers on the tension between his wolf family in Wolvendom and Mondstadt's Knights of Favonius.
canonical_facts.source: Razor Story Quest, Kindred by Blood chapter

canonical_facts.fact: Andrius remains an active, summonable boss encounter within Wolvendom in the current game; he is not depicted as a slain historical figure.

forbidden_claims: Wolf's Gravestone is confirmed in canon as the literal weapon that killed Andrius.
Andrius has died or been permanently defeated in the story.
Razor forged, named, or exclusively owns Wolf's Gravestone as a signature weapon.
Wolf's Gravestone is a unique quest reward rather than a generally obtainable five-star claymore.
Wolf's Gravestone possesses sentience, memory, or intent.

recent_hooks: A cursed Inazuman sword crossed nations by possessing successive human hosts.
This claymore is named Wolf's Gravestone — yet the wolf king it mourns has never died.
recent_fates: Reforged by Kazuha at the cost of its remaining consciousness, leaving the restored sword permanently silent.
Restored and carried into a Knights of Favonius armory, still bearing its grim name while Andrius and his forest endure.

episode_summaries.arc: Forged conscious in Snezhnaya by Akame Kanenaga, carried toward Inazuma through possessed hosts, weakened by the journey, and finally reforged by Kazuha at the cost of its consciousness.
episode_summaries.narrative_mode_used: External third-person lore narration about the item; the sword never narrates as itself.

episode_summaries.arc: Named for the human-wolf conflict in Mondstadt's Wolvendom and Andrius, the Wolf of the North; planted as a grave marker at the old battle site, later exhumed and restored by adventurers, its shockwave passive echoing the wolf pack's hunting instinct, ending in a Knights of Favonius armory while Andrius and his forest remain unresolved and very much alive.
episode_summaries.narrative_mode_used: External third-person lore narration about the item; the claymore never narrates as itself; no sentience implied.
episode_summaries.notes: Lesson: Scenarist's first monologue draft was 101 words for 7x5s=35s of picture; MiniMax rendered it at 60.6s (speed=0.85), a 73% overrun against the 40% masking cap in sound.md. Fixed two ways: trimmed narration to 83 words (dropping only secondary descriptive clauses, no canonical facts), and dropped MiniMax voice_setting.speed from 0.85 to 1.0 (the slowdown was itself inflating duration on top of the word count). Final TTS 44.42s against 35s picture = 1.26x atempo, within the 1.4x cap. Catch TTS/picture-duration mismatches at the Sound handoff, before Storyboarder/Animator spend.
